rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~5–10 at.% Re and applying helium-ion implantation during sputtering, whereas the paper compared equiatomic NbMoTaW with equiatomic NbMoTaWRe films and performed He implantation after deposition. The Re addition is the same kind of intervention, but the hypothesis adds an in-situ implantation step and a different Re concentration, making it a different specific lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature ductility testing and high-temperature strength up to 1600 °C, while the paper performed room-temperature nanoindentation and micropillar compression on films deposited at room temperature and irradiated at room temperature. The hypothesis includes a high-temperature regime not present in the paper, so only the room-temperature mechanical testing broadly aligns.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes altered grain boundary cohesion, dislocation mobility, and self-healing via enhanced atomic diffusion from helium-ion treatment. The paper's mechanism relies on Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth and segregation. These are different mechanistic pathways.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved room-temperature ductility, reduced irradiation defects, and maintained high-temperature strength. The paper found reduced irradiation hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement at room temperature, with no high-temperature testing. The direction of improved irradiation resistance aligns, but the hypothesis adds ductility and high-temperature strength predictions not tested in the paper.
